title: §.XII close: Royal rescript — Frederick orders Strimesius to declare Walther S.T.D.; Fuchs to Viadrina faculty
pass_a_gloss: But the Royal Rescript sounds thus: FREDERICK, by the Grace of God KING OF PRUSSIA, Margrave of Brandenburg, Arch-Chamberlain of the Holy Roman Empire and Prince Elector, Duke of Magdeburg, Cleves, Julich, Berg, Stettin, Pomerania, and so on. Reverend, Most Learned, Beloved and Faithful; Although the singular Erudition of M. Christian Walther, Pastor of Sackheim at Konigsberg in Prussia, recommended by you with no common praises, and the uprightness of his morals together with integrity of life, have already before this been clear to us, and We have been abundantly taught concerning his merits, so that even from this reason alone we would judge him by no means destitute of the honors desired; yet more has the rarest example thus far of a Lutheran Theologian seeking Theological Doctorate from Doctors of the Reformed faith with no less confidence than is their readiness and reciprocal zeal in promoting his desires incited us to assent to his vows and to your most humble prayers. This cannot but be most grateful to Us, since any wholesome and prosperous things for the Public as for the Ecclesiastical Commonwealth may thence be omened. We therefore not only Consent, but also command You, Samuel Strimesius, Dean of the Theological Faculty, and also Doctor and Ordinary Professor, and Primary Pastor of the Church, that you declare the aforesaid M. Christian Walther now indeed in Your Faculty Doctor of Sacred Theology, and in the next future Act of public Promotion proclaim and announce him such publicly, and make him partaker of all Privileges and Rights annexed to this highest title and belonging to Doctors of Theology through the Holy Roman Empire, which the Divine Numen may deign to second. Farewell, secure of Our Royal Grace. Given at Cologne on the Spree, the 20th day of March, Year 1702. FREDERICK THE KING. PAULUS, Freiherr de FUCHS. To the Theological Faculty of the Viadrina University.
pass_b_english: The royal rescript runs thus: Frederick, by God's grace King of Prussia, Margrave of Brandenburg, Arch-Chamberlain of the Holy Roman Empire and Prince Elector, Duke of Magdeburg, Cleves, Julich, Berg, Stettin, Pomerania, and so on.

Reverend, most learned, beloved and faithful: Walther's uncommon learning, upright manners, and integrity of life — praised by you without ordinary compliments — were already clear to us, and we know his merits well enough that on that ground alone we would not leave him without the honors he seeks.

What moved us still more to grant his wish and your humble petitions is this rare case: a Lutheran theologian seeking a theological doctorate from Reformed doctors with as much confidence as they show readiness and mutual zeal in advancing his desire.

That can only please us, since every wholesome good for the commonwealth and the church may be hoped from it. We therefore not only consent but command you, Samuel Strimesius — dean of the theological faculty, ordinary doctor and professor, and primary pastor — to declare M. Christian Walther now Doctor of Sacred Theology in your faculty, and at the next public promotion to proclaim him such, and to admit him to all privileges and rights belonging to that highest title and to doctors of theology in the Holy Roman Empire — which may God favor. Farewell, secure of our royal grace. Given at Cologne on the Spree, 20 March 1702.
Frederick the King. Paul, Freiherr von Fuchs. To the Theological Faculty of the Viadrina University.
source_text:
Rescriptum vero Regium ita sonat:
FRIDERICUS, D. G. REX BORUSSIAE,
Marchio Brandenburgensis, S. R. J. ArchiCamerarius & Princeps Elector, Magdeburgi, Cliviae, Juliae, Montium, Stetini, Pomeraniae &c. Dux &c.
Reverendi, Doctissimi, Dilecti ac Fideles;
Etsi jam antehac perspecta nobis sit M. Christiani Waltheri, Pastoris Sackheimensis Regiomonti Borussorum, haud vulgaribus elogiis à vobis commendati, singularis Eruditio, morum probitas juxta & vitae integritas, Nosque de meritis ejus affatim edoctissimi, adeò, ut vel ex hac sola ratione, illum exoptatis honoribus neutiquam destitutum censeamus; Magis tamen nos incitavit, ut votis ipsius, vestrisque humillimis annueremus precibus, rarissimum hactenus Theologi Lutherani exemplum, Docturam Theologicam à Reformatae fidei Doctoribus non minori fiducia expetentis, quàm horum in promovendis ejus desideriis est promptitudo & reciprocum studium. Non potest non Nobis hoc esse gratissimum, cùm salutaria quaevis ac prospera Rei, tàm Publicae, quàm Ecclesiasticae, inde ominari liceat. Consentimus itaque non solùm, verùm mandamus etiam Tibi, Samueli Strimesio, Facultatis Theologicae Decano, nec non Doctori & Professori Ordinario, ut & Pastori Ecclesiae Primario, ut praefatum M. Christianum Waltherum, nunc quidem in Facultate Vestra, S. S. Theologiae Doctorem declares, in proximo verò Promotionis publicae futuro Actu, talem publicè proclames & renuncies, omniumque Privilegiorum ac Jurium, summo huic Axiomati annexorum, ac Doctoribus Theologiae per S. R. J. competentium, participem reddas, quod Divinum Numen secundare dignetur. valete, de Gratia Nostra Regia securi. Dabantur Coloniae ad Svevum d. 20. Martii. Ao. 1702.

FRIDERICUS REX.

PAULUS, LIB. BARO de FUCHS.
Ad Facultatem Theologicam Universitatis Viadrinae.
